newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants to improve water use controls.
newsitem.headline: France wants to improve water use controls.

text.p: France's farm ministry will launch a nationwide debate on Tuesday on how to make controls over water use fairer and more effective, officials from farm development lobby Anda said on Monday.
Farm minister Phillipe Vasseur will detail "Operation Irrimieux" -- "Irrigate Better" -- at a news conference, they said.
Mounting drought fears have already led local authorities in 13 departments, including the Beauce grain belt, to slap limits on the amount of water farmers can use to irrigate their crops.
But farmers want restrictions over water use to be extended to cities and industries, although farming accounts for 41 percent of the nation's water consumption.
"Water control is becoming more and more necessary. It is clear that the drought has increased the need to control irrigation," Anda water expert Jean-Marie Berthout told Reuters.
"This situation is creating conflicts and the various parties involved must talk at a time when resources are limited," an official for the APCA farm lobby said.
The plan will cost around two million francs in 1997, which will be provided by the Environment and farm ministries.

A team of scientific and technical experts will head the project. A monitoring unit will regroup all parties involved in water control and wll make proposals at the local level. It will hold its first meeting in May.
France has already said it was putting an aid programme in place to compensate farmers for damage caused by drought and frost.
